description: Canonical registry for paper-local audits, formal propositions, empirical hypotheses, design principles, and open questions. Concept records remain in framework/concepts.json.

claims.name: Four-output audit
claims.proposition: Report integrity, rule conformance, policy sensitivity, and governance as separate outputs for adaptive mandates.

claims.name: Logical independence of integrity, conformance, and sensitivity
claims.proposition: Integrity and exact rule conformance do not imply zero policy sensitivity.

claims.name: Acceptance-criterion contrast
claims.proposition: When a scope rule counts acceptance of the system's own highlighted recommendation, changing the highlighting policy will change the probability of a widening transition more than it changes independent task-success criteria.

claims.name: Adaptive scope trajectory contrast
claims.proposition: Adaptive delegation based on agent-sensitive criteria produces different scope trajectories from delegation based on externally measured performance, even when immediate utility is similar.

claims.name: Review-burden contrast
claims.proposition: Frequent beneficiary-controlled review prompts increase approval while reducing attention and comprehension relative to batched, principal-controlled review.

claims.name: Immediate-source handoff loss
claims.proposition: If a handoff schema preserves only immediate source, then a truthful intermediate signature can hide a policy ancestor material to the authorization decision.

claims.name: Separate ancestry from predictive relevance
claims.proposition: An authorization service should not treat source authenticity or predictive relevance as sufficient for a widening transition when the prospective beneficiary materially controls causal ancestors of the evidence. It should record that ancestry and apply an influence policy or route the transition to review.

claims.name: Reference widening procedure
claims.proposition: For a proposed widening transition: authenticate the grant and evidence envelopes; validate role and jurisdiction separately from signature origin; replay the rule and enumerate exact added, removed, and incomparable permissions; retrieve evidence provenance and ancestry; evaluate the total policy contrast or declare it unidentified; check whether a prior grant governed the relevant influence and bounded the successor scope; when required, keep the prior valid scope while offering review through a refusal-capable channel; execute only the resulting authorized actions; and preserve scope attenuation, ancestry status, revocation, and appeal through subdelegation.

claims.name: Refusal-capable widening review
claims.proposition: Review for widening should preserve a visible “continue at prior scope” option, use symmetric acceptance and refusal effort, avoid unrelated bundling, disclose material evidence ancestry, and record prompt frequency and defaults. High-risk rights may require a user-controlled or institutionally separate review surface.

claims.name: Causal ancestry under compression
claims.proposition: What minimum metadata preserves a material policy ancestor when agents summarize, aggregate, anonymize, or learn from evidence? Full traces threaten privacy; short provenance chains lose causal content.

claims.name: Permission partial orders
claims.proposition: How should systems compare scopes with budgets, recipient sets, purposes, time windows, and subdelegation? Which transitions are widening, narrowing, or incomparable without inventing arbitrary scalar weights?

claims.name: Chosen formation
claims.proposition: How can a grant distinguish a person choosing to be coached from a provider declaring “coaching” after the fact? What evidence of comprehension and refusal is proportionate?

claims.name: Review independence
claims.proposition: When is a review channel sufficiently separate from the beneficiary? Must a different institution ratify, or can a user-controlled interface suffice? How should the answer vary with risk?

claims.name: Interference and collective authority
claims.proposition: How should policy effects be estimated when one person's agent changes a household, team, market, or public environment? Who defines the target population and represents non-principals?

claims.name: Strategic equilibria
claims.proposition: Do ancestry-aware rules reduce influence expenditure, move it to unobserved channels, or cause agents to avoid useful responsibility? Which commitments are stable?

claims.name: Real versus formal authority
claims.proposition: Can an audit combine typed permissions with measures of knowledge dependence, switching cost, initiative, and institutional control without pretending they share a single scale?

claims.name: Privacy-preserving audit
claims.proposition: Can zero-knowledge proofs, secure computation, aggregation, or trusted execution show that an evidence path satisfies a policy without exposing intimate behavioral traces?

claims.name: Artificial standing
claims.proposition: How would governance change if a delegate could have morally relevant interests or a claim to continuity? Which authority and revocation concepts remain valid?

claims.name: Cross-cultural validity
claims.proposition: Which role and authority assumptions are culturally contingent? What participatory methods can specify local jurisdiction without freezing existing domination into code?
